messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: INCIDENT 1809123456 - prod-inference p99 latency spike detected (>2.5s) in us-west-2. Alert: infra.alerts.inference_p99_high. Triggered 174 events in last 5m. Affected routes: /v1/generate. Paging team: @eng-oncall
Alex: grabbing logs, running quick checks. @Priya you'll want to join for infra.
Priya: on it. Checking autoscaling and GPU queue lengths.
Maya: seeing 503s coming from model-serving-4, KV cache miss rate super high. Might be cache thrash.
Diego: I can join — re-routing a portion of traffic to fallback model version now (model-1.2.3-canary).
Ken: routing change applied. Diverting 20% traffic off model-serving-4. Latency dipped for some requests.
Asha: customer impact: alpha-corp-prod seems to be 100% affected (ingest failures). beta-saas about 15% degraded. Notifying CS now.
Sora: I'm going to temporarily raise the alert threshold to reduce paging noise while we stabilize. Proposal: p99 threshold from 2.0s -> 3.5s for a 10m window with rate-of-change suppression.
Alex: +1 for temporary change. Documenting in ticket 3542. Post the rule we should apply to Alertmanager.
Priya: quick patch to test in staging: ```yaml
groups:
 - name: inference.rules
   rules:
   - alert: HighInferenceP99
     expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 3.5
     for: 10m
     labels:
       severity: warning
     annotations:
       summary: "Prod inference p99 high (>3.5s)"
```
Maya: scaled model pool +20% and triggered KV cache clear on serving nodes. Watching metrics.
oncall-bot: ACTION: reroute applied, autoscale adjusted, cache flush triggered.
Ken: 10m check-in: p99 down to ~1.2s. Looks stable from core infra POV. Leaving temporary threshold until post-incident review.
Diego: long-term proposals: add per-route p99 alerts + per-customer thresholds; map pages to customers with contractual SLAs. Example rule: page if (customers_affected >= 1 && error_rate > 1%) || p99 > 4s.
Asha: CS update: alpha-corp notified, preparing formal incident notification. No data loss reported, but possible SLA breach — flagged for account team.
Sora: I'll open a PR to formalize alert routing policy: separate logic for 'page' vs 'ticket', add channel mappings (sev1 -> #oncall-pager, sev2 -> #eng-alerts), and per-customer overrides. Also adding a per-customer heatmap to dashboard.
Alex: FYI handoff in 30m — Priya will take next oncall shift and own post-incident follow-up. Priya, you'll take ownership after the handoff.
Priya: ack, will take over. I'll update ticket 3542 with timeline and next steps. Planning RCA draft tomorrow.
Ken: follow-ups (created as checklist in ticket): 1) implement per-route throttling fallback 2) increase KV cache LRU and tune eviction 3) add canary drain logic for model deployments 4) update alerting docs with page/ticket mapping.
Maya: I'll build dashboard panels: p50/p95/p99 by route, by model version, per-customer error rate and affected-customer list. Will link in ticket.
Diego: creating RFC for severity mapping change and routing rules, tagging @eng-sre for review.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: status -> mitigated. Root cause investigation underway. Created follow-up channel #incidents/1809123456.
Alex: thanks everyone — leadership notified. Keeping ticket open until RCA and follow-up work complete.
